content:
I’m working on a little UX feature that will run try? for you whenever you have written by, but not actually started the proof. Here is what it looks like:

Video_2026-05-13_15-47-58.mp4

My assumption is that at least some user's workflow is to write a theorem including the ubiquitous := by, and then pause and think about their first step, and it would be great if lean could then jump in and say “Hey, I I can do that for you”, and you click and be done with it. If Lean can’t help you in this way, nothing happens, no distraction.

As try gets more powerful, this gets more powerful. I am in particular excited about lean telling you this way that a theorem is unprovable (using something like plausible, or by proving the opposite). Other systems have that, and it can be a big time saver if you notice early that there is something wrong with the lemma statement.

I believe this is a UX improvement, but I can’t tell for sure, primarily because I rarely do proofs with Lean these days. So I wonder if someone here is

  • excited about this feature
  • tends to work in areas where it is likely helpful (e.g. API development with careful simp and grind setups where then many theorems are rfl or simp or grind)
  • wants to be early adaptor
  • is willing to write not write := by sorry too quickly (see #lean4 > About the `sorry` habit )

The feature is currently on lean4 master. If you can use the latest nightly release for your project, then great, go ahead and enable it (set_option tactic.tryOnEmptyBy true in the file or -Dtactic.tryOnEmptyBy=true in the “Lean4 server options” settings of the VSCode extension). If you need to use a different version of lean I can backport this feature and give you a release you can use that should otherwise be identical to your release.

Any takers?

Joachim Breitner said:

  • excited about this feature

:raising_hand:

The biggest blocker for me is lack of Mathlib cache (which means I might be waiting for a few hours after every git switch before I can start proving things). Will this feature enter 4.30-rc3 and then we could try it in Mathlib?

Ah, and some of the feedback I’m interested in:

  • Does try? sometimes find a proof for you? Often enough to make a difference?
  • Does it surprise you with a proof, or is it only offering the proof you were about to write anyways?
  • Does the feature get in the way? (Noisy output, flickering, extra load on your machine)
  • Does the feature feel natural? Is “empty by” a good indication for “user is likely interested in unsolicited proof suggestions”?

Snir Broshi schrieb:

The biggest blocker for me is lack of Mathlib cache (which means I might be waiting for a few hours after every git switch before I can start proving things). Will this feature enter 4.30-rc3 and then we could try it in Mathlib?

If you know what you are doing you can set LEAN_GITHASH to make lake and the mathlib cache tool believe that you are still on the pristine toolchain, so that’s not a blocker. I don’t expect to be backporting this feature to actual RCs.

But sounds like I should prepare a branch off leanprover/lean4:v4.30.0-rc2 for mathlib people to use.

Joachim Breitner said:

  • Does the feature feel natural? Is “empty by” a good indication for “user is likely interested in unsolicited proof suggestions”?

I can answer this one without having used the feature: since an empty by gives an error, myself (and AFAIK others as well) always immediately write sorry afterwards. So unless these suggestions will also pop up for by sorry, this means that it only replaces typing try? with deleting the sorry to get suggestions, so I still have to intentionally ask for suggestions, just in a different manner.
Can you enable it for by sorry / any sorry, or is that too intrusive?

Snir Broshi schrieb:

since an empty by gives an error

Not any more! It’s not just an incomplete tactic script, just like by skip (since #13229).

I intentional did not enable this for by sorry because (at least for me) by sorry indicates “I’ll come that later”, not “I'm currently working on it”. I understand that everyone has different habits there, and maybe that’s precisely because of this “empty by is a parse error” issue, which I hope will soon be a forgotten thing from the past.

Joachim Breitner said:

Snir Broshi schrieb:

since an empty by gives an error

Not any more!

set_option tactic.tryOnEmptyBy true
theorem foo : True := by

still gives an unsolved goals error on Lean nightly (4.31.0-nightly-2026-05-13), wdym?
(also a bit awkward that trivial isn't suggested)
Right, but no longer a parse error, and you get to see the goal state. No more “unexpected end of input; expected '{'”.

So far I have not touched what try? actually does. trivial is a bag of not so trivial tactics, and while it’d be useful for proving True I wonder if there are real goals where trivial is useful but that isn’t covered by the other try? tactics.
2 messages were moved from this topic to #lean4 > About the `sorry` habit by Joachim Breitner.
You can use leanprover/lean4-pr-releases:pr-release-13724 instead of v4.30.0-rc2 to test this feature on mathlib.

If I'm on a fast machine then can I have lean spamming try? at all times and on all goals? And filling in proofs when it succeeds like cursor and these other autocomplete tools do (so it appears in grey by my cursor so I notice that the proof is done)?

That would be an interesting and bold extension of the idea. It may require more careful scheduling of work and maybe also, as you say, different UI for showing progresss and selecting proofs. And it blurs the like to what AI copilots can do better.
An alternative could be to have a scoped macro that redefines sorry to mean try? and, before you go to bed, you open the scope at the beginning of your file.

One option (not sure if this is a good idea or feasible to implement) is to add a command to VSCode's command palette (which users could bind to a keystroke) that runs try? on all sorrys in a file (or a selected region). Whenever it succeeds, it replaces the sorry with try? (the literal text try?, not with the result of a try?, because the users should be able to make their own selection). Importantly, this would be idempotent. I don't know if this would cause the whole file to be reparsed, or how to avoid performance issues from rechecking the same sorries at the start of the file a bunch of times when the user really just cares about some proof near the bottom of the file.
Then the new pattern (assuming sufficiently high performance) could be to start the theorem with by sorry, and then press Ctrl+something to see if it works.
The UX is a little different, but docs#Mathlib.TacticAnalysis.tryAtEachStep and the various linters derived from it seem pretty close.
Sounds like someone could build a “try at each sorry” on top of that?
Yes, very easily since it allows you to condition on the syntax.
Now you just need to hook into vscode's inline suggestion mechanism and Kevin has his “auto complete on all goals” feature :-)

I am intrigued by this feature, because my instinct is "it will hardly ever help" but I think my instinct is wrong and the truth is "it will sometimes help" e.g. it will spot when simp can close a goal when I'm still searching for relevant lemmas (and I suspect that this will be the main benefit in my corner of formalization, although perhaps when more things are tagged grind I'll find that grind becomes more useful for me). I also conjecture that I'm willing to pay for any potential sluggishness caused by this feature because I am lucky enough that I tend to only use Lean on powerful machines nowadays (and I am certainly not the only person in this luxurious state). Of course there's still a chance that the pain outweighs the benefits but I definitely think it's worth experimenting with! I always have copilot switched off in VS Code unless I am doing "mechanical" stuff because in general I don't find its suggestions useful, but "by the way, this line closes the goal in one go" is probably essentially always useful.

BTW, this feature has now reached mathlb, so you can use

set_option tactic.tryOnEmptyBy true

now! (Or add -Dtactic.tryOnEmptyBy=true in the “Lean4 server options” settings of the VSCode extension if you don't want to change the code.)

I am very interested in user feedback about this.

BTW, try now also tries the new impossible by simp (and by grind etc) to see if the these tactics can already determine that the goal is definitely not provable:

theorem foo : False := by
  impossible by simp

The combination of the two features may help you catch clearly bogus goal quickly I hope. And later down the line, we can include plausible in this setup.

Based on the discussion here (and in #lean4 > About the `sorry` habit ) I plan to expand the feature a bit more, once I have enough confidence in lean4#13830 and this reaches you, you can get auto-try on your choice of

  • empty proof blocks (including bullets and cases)
  • every incomplete proof block
  • every sorry

But I’m a bit reluctant without more evidence that this is actually helpful to some users.
